note: DESIGN NOTES — the two readings this node had to settle (Q1/Q2), and the two measurements behind them. (1) Q2 ANSWERED BY REVERSAL, NAMED: the .ann/archive/** snapshot commits in the SAME commit as the archive's live-tree deletions. 12/20 read the snapshot as the operator's deliverable and left it out of scope; measured live, that reading is what makes the engine's own archive dirty, because a renameSync is ONE change spanning two trees — half-staging it is not a smaller commit, it is a dirty tree that refuses the NEXT archive. engineWriteDirs() therefore names .ann/archive, and the reversal is pinned by test with the reason, not just the behaviour. (2) Q1 UNCHANGED: the delivery commit stays the operator's act — a source edit beside a tooling write commits the tooling path only and leaves the source dirty (re-asserted under the widened journal). (3) MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED — how git stages a removal: `git add -- <pathspec>` stages a removal for a pathspec naming a gone FILE even inside a mixed pathspec list, but a pathspec naming a gone (or present-but-empty) DIRECTORY stages NOTHING once mixed with other pathspecs (add, add -A and add -u all fail mixed; each works alone). A deletion record is therefore EXPANDED through `git ls-files -z -- <rel>` — the INDEX, never a worktree scan — with a fallback to the path itself. (4) MEASURED — a rename is invisible to `git show --name-only`: it collapses to the destination, so the e2e asserts on `--name-status` and takes BOTH halves. (5) EVERY PATH IS RESOLVED ON BOTH SIDES OF EVERY COMPARISON: the rules/ symlink points onto .ann/rules and git refuses a pathspec beyond a symbolic link, and the macOS temp dir is itself a symlink (/var to /private/var), so resolving one side only would make a real path look out of scope. (6) THE EXCLUSION SET IS A READABLE CONSTANT (neverStaged): the write-rev ledger and its .tmp, logs/** (the provider op-log records prompts), and the provider config (mode 0600, may hold the API key). A reviewer reads one list instead of reconstructing a predicate. (7) A REFUSED WRITE JOURNALS NOTHING — pinned per writer (an in-force spec name, a taken brief name, a bad staged-doc name): the journal is a fact about what was WRITTEN, so a refusal cannot claim a write it did not make. (8) FIXTURE CHANGE, HONESTLY NAMED: `docs --write` now moves HEAD, so the close-gesture e2e had to commit the deliverable BEFORE reading the sha it cites — the capture's own sha is the bytes the run saw (= HEAD at capture time), and a sha read any earlier would no longer bind (no-captured-pass). That is the fixture catching up to the new behaviour, not a weakened assertion.

claims.statement: The journal records a WRITE, not an event: WriteRecord carries `kind: 'write'|'delete'` plus a writer-derived `detail`, and `noteWrite` is called at the WRITE site, so a command that writes a file and lands NO event is still committed. The case the old journal structurally could not see is now pinned end to end: `docs --write` and `rules --write` land no event at all, and the new e2e asserts each commits its own file — a new commit whose subject is `docs: manifest (e2e)` / `rules: rules registry (e2e)` — while a READ of either view (the third e2e case) commits nothing. `writeDocsManifest` is the chokepoint every doc producer passes through (docs --write, spec!, a design brief, the goal doc, the archive), so one note there is what makes the manifest commit itself.

A deletion is a change: `archiveJourney` notes the legs removal (with the destination as `detail`) and the goal-doc removal as `kind: 'delete'`, and `stagedPaths()` expands each delete record through `git ls-files -z` — the INDEX, never a worktree scan — because it was MEASURED that a pathspec naming a gone DIRECTORY stages nothing once mixed with other pathspecs, while a pathspec naming a gone FILE stages its removal even mixed. The e2e runs the real binary against a real git fixture and asserts the archive is ONE commit whose subject is exactly `journey: archived · manifest — the session moved to <dest> (e2e)`, that the touched paths carry BOTH halves (a path under .ann/journey/legs and a path under .ann/archive, plus the removed docs/goal.md), and that the archive guard's own predicate — tracked porcelain lines under .ann/journey and .ann/archive, dropping `??` exactly as `uncommittedJourneyChanges()` does — is EMPTY afterwards. HONEST LIMIT: this is verified at the e2e seam (the real CLI + real git in a fixture), not by archiving the LIVE journey — that is the operator's structural reset, not mine to run.

The editor commits its own edit — pinned per writer, one test each: `writeGoalDoc` (goal doc + manifest) and `archiveJourney` in store.test.ts; a spec session's doc in spec-grill.test.ts; a design brief in design-brief.test.ts; staging an intent doc in intents.test.ts; `rules/check/rules.json` in the e2e. Every writer is also PINNED ON ITS REFUSAL: an in-force spec name, a taken brief name and a bad staged-doc name each journal NOTHING, so a refusal can never claim a write it did not make. 'A doc write leaves the tree clean' is asserted twice — `git status --porcelain` empty in the unit pin, and no tracked porcelain line under docs/ or the journey in the e2e. The symlink case is real, not hypothetical: `rules --write` writes through the shipped `rules -> .ann/rules` symlink, git refuses a pathspec beyond one, and the e2e proves the resolution by asserting the commit touched `.ann/rules/check/rules.json`.

The exclusions are a NAMED, readable list — `neverStaged(root)` — read by the staging filter, so a reviewer reads one decision instead of reconstructing a predicate: the write-rev ledger and its `.tmp`, `logs/**` (the provider op-log records prompts), and the provider config (mode 0600, may hold the API key).
